words.definition: Ready to do things that might be scary.
words.example_sentence: The brave dog jumped into the river to help.

words.definition: Very, very small.
words.example_sentence: A tiny ant carried a big crumb.

words.definition: Wanting to know or learn about something.
words.example_sentence: The curious cat looked inside the box.

words.definition: Soft and careful, not rough.
words.example_sentence: She was gentle when she held the baby bird.

words.definition: Doing good things for others.
words.example_sentence: The helpful boy picked up the toys.

words.definition: Able to recover quickly from difficulty.
words.example_sentence: The resilient team kept playing after three losses.

words.definition: To work together with others on something.
words.example_sentence: They chose to collaborate on the science project.

words.definition: Enough or satisfactory for the purpose.
words.example_sentence: Make sure you have adequate time to finish.

words.definition: To keep trying even when things are hard.
words.example_sentence: She chose to persevere until she understood it.

words.definition: Asking many questions; eager to learn.
words.example_sentence: The inquisitive student always had five questions.

words.definition: Open to more than one interpretation; unclear.
words.example_sentence: The ambiguous instructions confused the class.

words.definition: To understand and share the feelings of another.
words.example_sentence: A good leader must empathize with their team.

words.definition: To say or show the opposite of something.
words.example_sentence: His actions seemed to contradict everything he said.

words.definition: Expressing ideas clearly and fluently.
words.example_sentence: She gave an articulate speech that impressed everyone.

words.definition: A subtle difference in meaning or expression.
words.example_sentence: Understanding the nuance can change the meaning.

words.definition: To use ambiguous language to avoid commitment or deceive.
words.example_sentence: A skilled debater detects when opponents equivocate.

words.definition: To place two things side by side for contrast.
words.example_sentence: The author juxtaposed wealth and poverty in one chapter.

words.definition: Fluent and persuasive in speech or writing.
words.example_sentence: Her eloquent defence earned a standing ovation.

words.definition: A statement that contradicts itself yet may be true.
words.example_sentence: The paradox of freedom is that it can limit others.

words.definition: Dealing with things practically rather than theoretically.
words.example_sentence: A pragmatic approach to the crisis proved effective.
